newsitem.title: UK: Blast rocks English seaside town, no casualties.
newsitem.headline: Blast rocks English seaside town, no casualties.

text.p: An explosion rocked the main shopping street in the eastern English seaside town of Gorleston-on-Sea overnight but no one was injured, police said on Thursday.
The blast ripped through the front of one shop just before midnight (2400 GMT) on Wednesday, setting it and two nearby shops on fire.
"No one was injured. At this stage we do not know what the cause of the explosion was but it is being treated as suspicious," a police spokesman said.
British officials have warned of a possible fresh wave of Irish Republican Army (IRA) attacks on the British mainland.
On Tuesday, police launched an advertising campaign to encourage people to report suspicious activities to a confidential hotline.

"In the days and months ahead, we have reason to believe that the menace of terrorism, particularly in terms of murder, mayhem and damage to the public of Great Britain, remains," Assistant Commissioner of the Metropolitan Police David Veness told a news conference.
The advertising campaign followed reports last week that security services feared new attacks by the IRA before Christmas.
The IRA has planted seven bombs on the British mainland since abandoning a 17-month truce in February, citing British intransigence in the Northern Ireland peace process.

On February 9 a huge bomb rocked London's Docklands commercial district, killing two and injuring 100. In June, a bomb in a van exploded in a shopping centre in the northern English city of Manchester, injuring more than 200.
The police issued their latest warning despite recent successes against the IRA, who want a united Ireland and an end to rule from London.
Last month, police seized 100 tonnes of explosives and weapons in London raids and charged four people with conspiracy to cause explosions.

Police in the Irish Republic said on Monday they had seized a rocket launcher, explosives and weapons at what appeared to be an IRA guerrilla training camp. Five men were arrested and remanded in custody.
